branch_provenance.syndrome: Subacute Multisystem Syndrome with Mucocutaneous and Renal Involvement

state.case_summary:
A 70-year-old woman reported sudden warty growths over the lips with oral discomfort and difficulty eating. She had a 6-month history of vague abdominal discomfort.

Examination showed extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate. There were verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in the axillae, posterior neck, periumbilical region, and groin folds. Her palms had a ridged appearance and coarse texture with characteristic papillomatous appearance and accentuation of dermatoglyphics.

- Imaging Studies:    1. Abdominal CT:       - Finding: Large left-sided renal mass with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy    2. Thorax CT:        - Finding: Necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy causing superior vena cava compression        - Pathology:       - Radiologically guided biopsy of renal mass revealed invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation favoring a urothelial primary        - Clinical Images:       Figure 1. Clinical Image of Oral Lesions       Description: Diffuse, verrucous, and papillomatous plaques on the upper and lower lips; tongue has a diffuse, cobblestoned, papillomatous appearance              Figure 2. Clinical Images of Palm Lesions       Description: Both palms showing characteristic ridged papillomatous appearance and coarse texture with accentuation of dermatoglyphics

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Paraneoplastic Syndrome with Transitional Cell Carcinoma
B. Stage IV invasive renal urothelial carcinoma
C. Florid Cutaneous Papillomatosis with Urothelial Cancer
D. Metastatic urothelial carcinoma (renal pelvis) with paraneoplastic malignant acanthosis nigricans

excluded_candidates: infectious etiology: unlikely due to presence of invasive carcinoma
autoimmune disorder: possible but less likely given the presence of renal mass and lymphadenopathy
